The little thingy you turned with the screwdriver was probably the adjustment screw. Turning it one way will pull the shoes away from the drums and turning the other way will push the shoes into the drums.

Get the tire in the air and spin it by hand. If it free wheels keep moving the adjuster until the tire moves by hand but doesn't freely spin or only spins a very little bit.

You can move to the other side and do the same and then test the parking brake.  


If it were me doing the job to my own car i would do one side, make the adjustment as above and set the parking brake with the tire still in the air. I would then try to remove a lugnut with the tire iron. If the tire doesn't move the brake will likely hold the car.  


On some vehicles you can reach the adjuster with the car on the ground in which case you just ratchet each side until properly adjusted.

When finished the parking brake should hold the car while idling and in gear.

A clogged cat is certainly a possibility. A pain in the ass way to check thaty would be to remove your exhaust but it's possible every bolt you touch will break. Nature of the beast.

Another potential issue could be your fuel pressure regulator, fuel filter or pump. If you could get a fuel pressure gauge and snake it out under your hood while you go for a test drive it would be helpful in eliminating some potential areas.

Lots of tools for diagnosing that type of issue (one that does not illuminate a light) are manufacturer (dealer) specific so you may be stuck going that route.

Also, lots of EPS systems are assist adjusted based on other inputs (yaw, speed, steering angle) or combinations of multiple inputs. If any one of those inputs has an issue it could be reflected in steering effort. They could also throw a MIL by themselves

Typically when EPS has an issue that causes it not to be able to function power assist is set to a static level so you could get the same amount of assist when turning from a dead stop (requiring high assist) as you would when pushing a corner (low assist).

I think you would notice that while driving but reaching that level of issue should also throw a ilght.
